item.title: 1,295 residents leave Fiji for employment in July
item.description: A total of 1,295 Fiji residents departed the country for employment purposes in July 2026, according to the latest resident departure figures. The data shows employment accounted for 8.3 per cent of the 15,694 resident departures recorded during the month.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 1,295 Fiji residents departed the country for employment purposes in July 2026, according to the latest resident departure figures.

The data shows employment accounted for 8.3 per cent of the 15,694 resident departures recorded during the month.

Of those leaving for employment, 287 were expected to be away for less than three months, while 489 indicated an absence of between three and 12 months.

Another 519 residents left for employment for periods ranging from one to five years, the largest group among employment-related departures.

Overall, 13,665 residents, or 87.1 per cent of all departures, indicated they would be away for less than three months.

Holiday travel remained the leading reason for residents leaving Fiji, accounting for 6,497 departures or 41.4 per cent.

Another 5,278 residents departed to visit friends or relatives, while 983 travelled for business and 800 for education or training.

The figures also show 148 residents departed for emigration, including 91 who indicated they would be away for more than five years or permanently.

item.title: Fiji records highest-ever monthly visitor arrivals
item.description: Fiji recorded its highest monthly visitor arrivals on record in July 2026, with the number of visitors surpassing 100,000 for the first time. Provisional figures released by the Fiji Bureau of Statistics show 105,791 visitors arrived during the month, up 6.5 per cent from the 99,311 recorded in July last year.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji recorded its highest monthly visitor arrivals on record in July 2026, with the number of visitors surpassing 100,000 for the first time.

Provisional figures released by the Fiji Bureau of Statistics show 105,791 visitors arrived during the month, up 6.5 per cent from the 99,311 recorded in July last year.

The latest result continues an upward trend in July arrivals, which increased from 78,638 in 2022 to 93,483 in 2023 and 98,332 in 2024.

Of the 105,791 visitors recorded last month, 104,377 arrived by air and 1,414 by sea. Sea arrivals included 914 seamen from fishing vessels and 500 visitors arriving by yacht.

Holidaymakers continued to dominate the market, accounting for 80.1 per cent of all arrivals. Another 8.7 per cent came to visit friends or relatives, 1.6 per cent travelled for business and 9.6 per cent visited for other reasons.

Australia remained Fiji’s largest source market, contributing 45,907 visitors, or 43.4 per cent of total arrivals.

New Zealand followed with 28,430 visitors, representing 26.9 per cent, while the United States contributed 13,428 visitors, or 12.7 per cent.

Continental Europe recorded 3,117 visitors, China 3,093, Canada 1,722 and the United Kingdom 1,393.

Together, Fiji’s major source markets accounted for 91.8 per cent of all July arrivals.

The statistics also show 59.3 per cent of visitors were aged between 25 and 64, while children aged 14 and below accounted for 18.3 per cent.

Youths aged between 15 and 24 represented 11.6 per cent, while visitors aged 65 and over accounted for the remaining 10.8 per cent.

item.title: 743 new overseas voters registered through FEO overseas outreach
item.description: A total of 743 new overseas voters have been registered through the Fijian Elections Office’s voter registration outreach programmes conducted overseas in 2025 and 2026. The figures were tabled in Parliament yesterday by Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga in response to a written question from MP Inosi Kuridrani on the FEO’s voter awareness and registration programmes.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 743 new overseas voters have been registered through the Fijian Elections Office’s voter registration outreach programmes conducted overseas in 2025 and 2026.

The figures were tabled in Parliament yesterday by Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga in response to a written question from MP Inosi Kuridrani on the FEO’s voter awareness and registration programmes.

According to the parliamentary response, 468 new voters were registered through overseas outreach in 2025, while another 275 new registrations were recorded through the 2026 programme.

In 2025, the FEO conducted registration activities in the United Kingdom, Tuvalu, Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands, Samoa, American Samoa, the United States, Solomon Islands, Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia and Hawaii.

The 2026 overseas programme included Nauru, Tonga, New Zealand, Australia, the United States, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Kiribati, Hawaii, Canada and Palau.

New Zealand recorded the highest number of new registrations during the 2026 outreach with 90, followed by Australia with 50, the United States with 43 and Canada with 41.

The figures also show that overseas registration services involved significantly more than just new voters.

In 2025, the overseas programme recorded 2,205 total registrations, comprising 468 new registrations and 1,738 corrections and replacements, as reported in the table.

For 2026, there were 1,901 total registrations, including 275 new registrations and 1,626 corrections and replacements.

Meanwhile, the FEO’s nationwide YES Outreach voter registration drive from May 4 to June 19 this year recorded 8,158 new registrations.

The nationwide drive also processed 61,723 corrections and updates and 28,091 replacements, bringing the accumulated total to 97,972 voter registration transactions.

item.title: 682 Justices of the Peace serving across Fiji
item.description: There are currently 682 active Justices of the Peace in Fiji, with Government acknowledging that several maritime and interior areas still need greater access to JP services. The figures were tabled in Parliament today by Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga in response to a written question from MP Sakiusa Tubuna.
item.content:encoded:
There are currently 682 active Justices of the Peace in Fiji, with Government acknowledging that several maritime and interior areas still need greater access to JP services.

The figures were tabled in Parliament today by Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga in response to a written question from MP Sakiusa Tubuna.

According to the response, the Central/Eastern Division has the largest number of JPs with 339, followed by the Western Division with 271 and the Northern Division with 72.

Of the total, 33 JPs are located in the Maritime Region, including 10 in Lomaiviti, nine in Lau, six in Taveuni, five in Kadavu and one each in Beqa, Vatulele and Yasawa.

However, Government acknowledged there were still areas where JP numbers were limited or additional appointments were needed.

These include Yasawa, Yacata, Cikobia, Kadavu, Yanuca and Rotuma, as well as interior areas in Namosi, Naitasiri, Ba, Navosa, Macuata, Cakaudrove and Bua.

“The distribution of JPs highlights the need to continue strengthening access to JP services, particularly in remote, maritime and interior communities,” the parliamentary response stated.

JPs receive a $100 monthly allowance, subject to submitting monthly reports and providing services to a minimum quota of 50 customers per month where applicable.

A total of $477,100 was paid in JP allowances during the 2025–2026 financial year, while $600,000 has been allocated for the current financial year.

The Government is also preparing to appoint another 30 JPs.

Processing of applications for the next round of appointments began this month, with 30 applicants expected to be appointed.

From the current financial year, new JP appointments will be limited to 30 applicants annually, with appointments primarily targeted at areas where a need for additional JP services has been identified.

item.title: Rabuka eyes appeal
item.description: PRIME Minister Sitiveni Rabuka is seriously considering appealing a High Court judgment that nullified the Commission of Inquiry (COI) report, saying any challenge would focus only on findings relating to his actions. Mr Rabuka said his decision would depend on advice from his legal counsel.
item.content:encoded:
PRIME Minister Sitiveni Rabuka is seriously considering appealing a High Court judgment that nullified the Commission of Inquiry (COI) report, saying any challenge would focus only on findings relating to his actions.

Mr Rabuka said his decision would depend on advice from his legal counsel.

Justice Dane Tuiqereqere found that Mr Rabuka, the President and the COI Commissioner had breached the principles of natural justice, ruling that people affected by adverse findings in the report should have been given an opportunity to respond before decisions were made based on those findings.

Mr Rabuka maintained that he had acted on legal advice after making recommendations following the COI.

He said the President had acted on his advice and that he accepted responsibility for his actions.

“The President only acts on advice, so the onus is on me, not him,” Mr Rabuka said.

He said the COI report and its recommendations were first provided to the President before being returned to him, after which he passed the recommendations to authorities empowered to bring charges.

Mr Rabuka said those facing charges would have an opportunity to defend themselves through the courts.

“I have no right to give any right to respond to anybody,” he said.

He said the charges were based on recommendations from COI Commissioner Justice David Ashton-Lewis and counsel assisting Janet Mason, and had been approved by legal officers from the Solicitor-General’s Office and the Attorney-General.

Mr Rabuka said the matter would proceed through the appeals process.

“At the end of it, there will be an appeal. It goes up to the Court of Appeals.”

He said the matter could ultimately reach the Supreme Court if he was dissatisfied with the outcome of the appeal.

item.title: Sekiseki puts climate justice in spotlight
item.description: FOR Salanieta Sekiseki, leadership is not something she hopes to learn on a stage. It already began at home, where as the eldest of six siblings, she learned early that leadership comes with responsibility, service and setting an example for others.
item.content:encoded:
FOR Salanieta Sekiseki, leadership is not something she hopes to learn on a stage.

It already began at home, where as the eldest of six siblings, she learned early that leadership comes with responsibility, service and setting an example for others.

That upbringing shaped the 23-year-old final-year law student’s journey to the Hibiscus Festival, where she hopes to turn her sense of responsibility into a platform for change.

Ms Sekiseki proudly hails from Bua Lomanikoro and has maternal links to Funafou in Malaita, Solomon Islands.

Growing up in a large family, she says her parents taught her to remain humble, courageous and resilient in the face of life’s challenges.

“As the oldest child of six siblings, I have a strong sense of responsibility, and that responsibility has been my greatest teaching,” she said.

At the festival, Ms Sekiseki will advocate for climate justice, environmental sustainability and youth empowerment.

She hopes to encourage young people to use the tools and resources available to them to speak up on environmental and climate issues.

She says the festival is more than a competition for a crown.

It is an opportunity to bring grassroots concerns to a national platform while encouraging more young women to use their voices and make a difference.

item.title: A call to traditional leaders
item.description: THE Ministry of Health is calling on traditional leaders to play an active role in combatting the country’s escalating HIV crisis, following warnings that current case numbers reflect only a fraction of the actual situation. Speaking at the 2026 HIV Pacific Symposium at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi yesterday, Health and Medical Services Minister Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu stressed
item.content:encoded:
THE Ministry of Health is calling on traditional leaders to play an active role in combatting the country’s escalating HIV crisis, following warnings that current case numbers reflect only a fraction of the actual situation.

Speaking at the 2026 HIV Pacific Symposium at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi yesterday, Health and Medical Services Minister Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu stressed that curbing transmission required a unified, nationwide effort.

His comments echoed an earlier address by the President, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, who highlighted the critical involvement of the vanua, the traditional indigenous socio-political structure, in tackling the health emergency.

“Our endeavour is to reduce transmission and try to get control of our epidemics,” Dr Lalabalavu said. He emphasised that traditional structures must be integrated into national strategy.

“We need everyone, including the vanua, an integral part of our effort to do this. Definitely, coming from his Excellency the President, that speaks volumes.”

Dr Lalabalavu said the president’s call to action as both head of state and a traditional leader sets a precedent for community engagement.

“For me, as with the current taskforce and this program, there is a place for the vanua at the table to see how best we can discuss these things moving forward.”

Addressing global targets aimed at controlling HIV by 2030, he said achieving progress depended entirely on effective local execution rather than passive goal-setting.

“While the target is there, how it can be achieved is dependent on how the programs are fully implemented.”

With testing efforts expanding across the country, official case numbers continue to climb, a trend the minister described as an essential first step toward long-term control. “As the excellency said, this is just the tip of the iceberg, right now, while the numbers keep increasing, our efforts should also scale up in terms of treatment, testing and awareness.”

item.title: Peceli found guilty of murder
item.description: The High Court in Lautoka has found Mokani, Tailevu native Peceli Rokoravolo guilty of killing prominent Nadi doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya. Lautoka High Court Judge Justice Aruna Aluthge delivered a lengthy judgment this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The High Court in Lautoka has found Mokani, Tailevu native Peceli Rokoravolo guilty of killing prominent Nadi doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya.

Lautoka High Court Judge Justice Aruna Aluthge delivered a lengthy judgment this afternoon.

Mr Rokoravolo is charged with the murder of Dr Biumaitotoya, who was commonly known on social media as Dr Leli Darling, between August 31 and September 1,2025, in Nadi.

Dr Biumaitotoya died from severe traumatic head injuries caused by multiple chop wounds.
